mn131:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
mn131:1.3: There he addressed the bhikkhus thus:
mn131:2.1: ‘Bhikkhus, I shall give you a summary and an exposition of one who has a single fortunate attachment.
mn131:2.2: Listen and heed well what I shall say.’
mn131:3.1: ‘Let not a man revive the past
mn131:3.2: or on the future build his hopes;
mn131:3.5: Rather with insight let him see
mn131:3.8: let him know it and be sure of it.
mn131:3.9: Today the effort must be made;
mn131:3.10: tomorrow Death may come, who knows?
mn131:3.12: can keep him and his hordes away.
mn131:3.13: But one who dwells thus ardently,
mn131:3.15: it is he, the peaceful sage has said,
mn131:3.16: who has a single fortunate attachment.
mn131:4.1: ‘And how, bhikkhus, does one revive the past?
mn131:4.2: Thinking, “I had such form in the past,” he allows himself to relish that; thinking, “I had such feeling in the past,” he allows himself to relish that; thinking, “I had such perception in the past,” he allows himself to relish that; thinking, “I had such formations in the past,” he allows himself to relish that; thinking, “I had such consciousness in the past,” he allows himself to relish that—
mn131:4.3: that, bhikkhus, is how one revives the past.
mn131:5.1: ‘And how, bhikkhus, does one not revive the past?
mn131:5.2: Thinking, “I had such form in the past,” he does not allow himself to relish that; thinking, “I had such feeling in the past,” he does not allow himself to relish that; thinking, “I had such perception in the past,” he does not allow himself to relish that; thinking, “I had such formations in the past,” he does not allow himself to relish that; thinking, “I had such consciousness in the past,” he does not allow himself to relish that—
mn131:5.3: that, bhikkhus, is how one does not revive the past.
mn131:6.1: ‘And how, bhikkhus, does one build up hope upon the future?
mn131:6.2: Thinking, “May my form be such in the future,” he allows himself to relish that; may my feeling be such … may my perception be such … may my formations be such … thinking, “May my consciousness be such in the future,” he allows himself to relish that—
mn131:6.3: that, bhikkhus, is how one builds up hope upon the future.
mn131:7.1: ‘And how, bhikkhus, does one not build up hope upon the future?
mn131:7.2: Thinking, “May my form be such in the future,” he does not allow himself to relish that; may my feeling be such … may my perception be such … may my formations be such … thinking, “May my consciousness be such in the future,” he does not allow himself to relish that—
mn131:7.3: that, bhikkhus, is how one does not build up hope upon the future.
mn131:8.1: ‘And how, bhikkhus, is one vanquished in regard to presently arisen dhammas?
mn131:8.2: Here, bhikkhus, the untaught ordinary man, who has no regard for the Noble Ones and is unconversant with their Dhamma and undisciplined in it, who has no regard for True Men and is unconversant with their Dhamma and undisciplined in it,
mn131:8.3: sees form as self, or self as possessed of form, or form in self, or self in form;
mn131:8.7: he sees consciousness as self, or self as possessed of consciousness, or consciousness in self, or self in consciousness—
mn131:8.8: that, bhikkhus, is how one is vanquished in regard to presently arisen dhammas.
mn131:9.1: ‘And how, bhikkhus, is one not vanquished in regard to presently arisen dhammas?
mn131:9.2: Here, bhikkhus, the well-taught disciple of the Noble Ones, who has regard for the Noble Ones and is conversant with their Dhamma and disciplined in it, who has regard for True Men and is conversant with their Dhamma and disciplined in it,
mn131:9.3: does not see form as self, or self as possessed of form, or form in self, or self in form;
mn131:9.7: he does not see consciousness as self, or self as possessed of consciousness, or consciousness in self, or self in consciousness—
mn131:9.8: that, bhikkhus, is how one is not vanquished in regard to presently arisen dhammas.
mn131:10.1: ‘Let not a man revive the past
mn131:10.2: or on the future build his hopes;
mn131:10.5: Rather with insight let him see
mn131:10.8: let him know it and be sure of it.
mn131:10.9: Today the effort must be made;
mn131:10.10: tomorrow Death may come, who knows?
mn131:10.12: can keep him and his hordes away.
mn131:10.13: But one who dwells thus ardently,
mn131:10.15: it is he, the peaceful sage has said,
mn131:10.16: who has a single fortunate attachment.
mn131:11.1: ‘“Bhikkhus, I shall give you a summary and an exposition of one who has a single fortunate attachment”—
mn131:11.2: so it was said, and it was with reference to this that it was said.’
mn131:11.3: This is what the Blessed One said.
mn131:11.4: The bhikkhus were satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
